title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
The latest USDA Crop report, issued Monday, says that 8% of the corn crop is harvested with 58% in good to excellent condition, 88% dented, and 50% mature, while 4% of soybeans are harvested with 57% in good shape and 46% dropping leaves.  One percent of winter wheat is planted.

The USDA reported Monday that there were 6.3 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending August 13th.  The average temperature was 77.7 degrees, 6.4 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 1.55 inches, .75 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 11% very short, 29% short, 58% adequate and 2% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 11% very short, 32% short, 56% adequate, and 1% surplus.

Corn dough reached 88%, compared to the 5-year average of 87%.  Corn dented reached 50%, compared to the 5-year average of 46%.  Corn Harvested is at 8%, compared to the 5-year average of 4%.  Corn condition was rated 4% very poor, 9% poor, 29% fair, 44% good, and 14% excellent.

Soybeans dropping leaves reached 46%, compared to the 5-year average of 43%.  Soybeans harvested reached 4% compared to the 5-year average of 2%.  Soybeans condition was rated 5% very poor, 8% poor, 30% fair, 43% good, and 14% excellent.

Winter Wheat planted in Illinois reached 1% even with the 5-year average.

title: IFB ISSUES ACTION REQUEST
full_story:
In anticipation of the farm bill markup this week by the Senate Agriculture Committee, Illinois Farm Bureau launched an action request Monday urging Senator Dick Durbin to support the legislation.

The current farm bill, which has been extended several times by Congress since 2023, expires on September 30th.  The House passed its version of a bill in April, but the Senate bill failed to advance out of committee in August.

The action request targets Durbin, as he serves on the Senate Ag Committee.

With few working days left in this congressional session, farm groups are pushing for swift passage out of committee.  IFB members also will be in Washington, DC this week and will urge members of Congress to advance the farm bill.

As of Monday morning, Senate Ag Committee Chair John Boozman, had not scheduled the markup.

Despite the bipartisan amendment process during the August 6th committee meeting, the bill ultimately failed to advance because of partisan disagreements over the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program state cost-share provisions.

The legislation updates key farm bill programs that have not been revised since Congress last passed a comprehensive farm bill in 2018.  The Senate bill also provides for nationwide year-round E15 sales.

title: AIRPORT GRANTS
full_story:
US Representative Mike Bost announced that the Federal Aviation Administration awarded grants totaling over $2.3 million to enhance safety and infrastructure improvements at Veterans Airport in Marion and MidAmerica Airport in Mascoutah.

“Southern Illinois is emerging as a transportation hub for our region, and Veterans Airport and MidAmerica Airport are critical transportation assets,” said Bost.  “These investments will help ensure both airports have safe and reliable infrastructure they need to continue protecting travelers and creating economic opportunities for the region.”

Veterans Airport will receive $1,176,548 to purchase a new aircraft rescue and firefighting vehicle, along with protective equipment and medical kits to enhance safety.  MidAmerica Airport will receive $1,149,763 to bring the surrounding landscape into conformity with current FAA standards.

title: ODELL JOINS FMH
full_story:
Fairfield Memorial Hospital announced Dr. Sean Odell, orthopedic surgeon, has joined its medical staff as an independent contractor.  Dr. Odell is a board-certified orthopedic surgeon who is fellowship trained and board certified in sports medicine and arthroscopic surgery.  He specializes in the treatment of complex injuries of the shoulder and knee, while also providing comprehensive orthopedic care for patients of all ages.

Dr. Odell completed an additional year of fellowship training in sports medicine at the Ohio Orthopedic Center of Excellence.  During his fellowship, he gained specialized experience treating orthopedic and sports-related conditions, including providing care for athletes with the Columbus Crew, a Major League Soccer team, as well as numerous high school athletes.

Dr. Odell provides both nonsurgical and surgical treatment options, based on each patient’s individual condition, symptoms, lifestyle and treatment goals.

Dr. Odell’s ultimate goal is to help patients safely return to their daily activities, work or competitive sports as quickly as possible.  His collaborative and educational approach allows patients to better understand their condition and participate in decisions regarding their treatment.

Dr. Odell will work collaboratively with Physician Assistant John Nugent to provide comprehensive orthopedic care to patients in the region.  Together, they will help patients receive convenient access to orthopedic evaluation, treatment and follow-up care close to home.

Dr. Odell will see patients every other Friday on the second floor of the Surgical Pavilion, located at 303 NW 11th Street in Fairfield.

To schedule an appointment or learn more about orthopedic services, call 618-919-4020.

title: FORD RECALL
full_story:
Ford Motor Company is recalling 223,472 vehicles in the US due to leaky and improperly secured fuel tanks that may detach from the vehicle while driving, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said.

A detached tank can create a road hazard, increasing the risk of a crash, while a fuel leak can cause an engine stall or increase the risk of a fire, according to a NHTSA advisory.

Certain 2023-2027 F-150 vehicles will be recalled due to this concern.  Dealers will inspect and replace the fuel tank straps, as necessary, free of charge.
